description: This chapter explains what cells are, how they were discovered, and how they are organised inside. It covers the cell membrane, nucleus, organelles, and how cells divide — because every living thing is made of cells, and understanding them is the foundation of biology.

sections.title: 5.1 What are Living Organisms Made Up Of?
sections.summary: Discovery of cells, unicellular vs multicellular organisms, cell theory, and the concept of division of labour within a cell
diagrams: Figure 5.2 — Cells of an onion peel
Figure 5.3 — Various cells from the human body

sections.title: 5.2 What is a Cell Made Up Of? — Structural Organisation of a Cell
sections.summary: Three main features of every cell — plasma membrane, nucleus, and cytoplasm — and how they work together

subsections.title: 5.2.1 Plasma Membrane or Cell Membrane
subsections.summary: Structure and function of the plasma membrane, diffusion, osmosis, tonicity, endocytosis, and membrane composition

subsections.title: 5.2.2 Cell Wall
subsections.summary: Plant cell wall composition (cellulose), its role in structural strength, and plasmolysis in living plant cells

subsections.title: 5.2.3 Nucleus
subsections.summary: Structure of the nucleus, nuclear membrane, chromosomes, DNA, genes, chromatin, prokaryotes vs eukaryotes, and the nucleoid

subsections.title: 5.2.5 Cell Organelles
subsections.summary: Overview of membrane-bound organelles in eukaryotic cells — ER, Golgi apparatus, lysosomes, mitochondria, plastids, and vacuoles

subsections.title: 5.2.5 (i) Endoplasmic Reticulum (ER)
subsections.summary: Structure of ER, rough vs smooth ER, ribosomes, membrane biogenesis, and functions in transport and detoxification

subsections.title: 5.2.5 (ii) Golgi Apparatus
subsections.summary: Structure of Golgi apparatus (cisterns), its role in packaging/modification/dispatch, and Camillo Golgi's contributions

subsections.title: 5.2.5 (iii) Lysosomes
subsections.summary: Structure and function of lysosomes as waste disposal system, suicide bags concept

subsections.title: 5.2.5 (iv) Mitochondria
subsections.summary: Structure (double membrane, folded inner membrane), ATP production, mitochondria as powerhouse with own DNA and ribosomes

subsections.title: 5.2.5 (v) Plastids
subsections.summary: Types of plastids (chromoplasts, leucoplasts, chloroplasts), their roles in photosynthesis and storage, internal structure (stroma)

subsections.title: 5.2.5 (vi) Vacuoles
subsections.summary: Vacuoles as storage sacs, differences between plant and animal cell vacuoles, cell sap and turgidity

sections.title: Cell Division
sections.summary: Two types of cell division — mitosis (growth/repair, two identical daughter cells) and meiosis (gamete formation, four cells with half chromosomes)

sections.title: What You Have Learnt
sections.summary: Chapter summary — key points about cell structure, membrane, organelles, prokaryotic vs eukaryotic cells, and cell division

sections.title: Exercises
sections.summary: 10 practice questions covering comparisons, organelle functions, osmosis experiments, and cell division types
